overdue-and-large.formatSuggestion: Light red fill (#FFC7CE) with dark red text (#9C0006)
stepsExcel: Select A2:G200, starting from A2.
Home > Conditional Formatting > New Rule.
Choose “Use a formula to determine which cells to format” and paste the formula.
Click Format…, choose the fill colour, then OK > OK.
stepsSheets: Select A2:G200.
Format > Conditional formatting.
Under “Format cells if…”, choose “Custom formula is” and paste the formula.
Pick the formatting style, then Done.
notes: The $ before E and D keeps every cell of a row looking at columns E and D; the row number moves down row by row.
assumptions: Amounts in column D are numbers, not text.
Status is spelled exactly Overdue (upper and lower case do not matter).

notes: Both copies of a repeated name are highlighted.
assumptions: Names are spelled the same way in each row; extra spaces make them different.

stepsExcel: Select C2:C300, starting from C2.
Data > Data Validation.
Settings tab: Allow “List”, then fill in the formula or source.
Error Alert tab: Style “Stop”, then OK.
stepsSheets: Select C2:C300.
Data > Data validation > Add rule.
Criteria: “Dropdown (from a range)” and paste the formula or range.
Advanced options: “Reject the input”, then Done.
notes: Excel 2010 and later accept a list on another sheet directly.
assumptions: The list has no blank cells in the middle.

stepsExcel: Select D2:D400, starting from D2.

Settings tab: Allow “Custom”, then fill in the formula or source.
Error Alert tab: Style “Stop”, then OK.
stepsSheets: Select D2:D400.
Data > Data validation > Add rule.
Criteria: “Custom formula is” and paste the formula or range.
Advanced options: “Reject the input”, then Done.
notes: Excel's built-in Allow: Date, between 1/1/2026 and 12/31/2026 does the same.
assumptions: Dates are real dates, not text.

notes: Without regular expressions the check is approximate: it tests the length, the capitals, the dash and four digits, but not that each of the first three characters is a letter.
assumptions: Letters are A to Z without accents.

stepsSheets: Select C2:C500.
Format > Conditional formatting.
Under “Format cells if…”, choose “Custom formula is” and paste the formula.
Pick a fill colour, then Done.
notes: The pattern is approximate: it finds 11-character values with dashes in positions 4 and 7 and digits elsewhere. These are personal data: delete or mask them, and remember earlier versions of the file may still hold them.
assumptions: The numbers are stored as text with dashes.
